title: Allow traffic from a specific IP address or subnet with UFW
summary: Configure the UFW firewall to accept connections only from a specific source IP address or a range of addresses (subnet). This is useful for restricting access to trusted networks or devices.

steps.explain: Allow all incoming traffic from a specific source IP address. Replace <SOURCE_ADDRESS> with the IP address you want to trust.

placeholders.name: SOURCE_ADDRESS
placeholders.description: The IP address to allow traffic from

steps.explain: Alternatively, allow traffic from an entire subnet using CIDR notation. This example allows all devices in the 192.168.13.0/24 network.

alternatives.explain: Allow traffic from a specific source IP to a specific destination IP on a specific port and protocol.
alternatives.cmd: sudo ufw allow from <SOURCE_IP> to <DEST_IP> port <PORT> proto <PROTOCOL>

alternatives.explain: Allow traffic on a specific interface to a specific destination IP for a specific protocol.
alternatives.cmd: sudo ufw allow in on <INTERFACE> to <DEST_IP> proto <PROTOCOL>

rollback.explain: To remove the rule, use the delete command with the same parameters.

warnings: Be careful when allowing entire subnets; ensure you trust all devices in that range.
Incorrect IP addresses may block legitimate traffic or allow unauthorized access.
